summary.overall_assessment: High-quality dataset. Every id, count, amount, product, status, date, history step and failure reason was recomputed by hand from spec sections 5.1-5.2. None of the structured expectations is wrong. Reference aggregates: 10 paid, 3 expired, 3 failed, 3 open, 1 creation_unknown. Collected gross is 444.70 (Pro 179.40 / 6 units, Starter 69.30 / 7 units, Report 196.00 / 4 units). Recovered = P08 only. Paid after expiry = P14 only. Confirmed by reconciliation = P08 only. All of these agree with the oracle, and documentation key facts agree with section 9. The problems are interpretive. Two answerable cases have a reasonable second reading with a different number and do not declare it: q038 ('came in' = created vs paid) and q063 ('ha comprato' = any status vs paid). Several other cases record an alternative reading only in notes instead of in interpretations (q062, q079, r016), or rely on a definition a merchant may not share (q059, q061, q091). Schema use is inconsistent for quantity > 1: null in q035/q063 but {gt:1} in r008. q079 uses measure 'list' while expecting a sum. Expected behaviours match section 6 throughout. Other-merchant id lookups correctly expect no_match rather than refuse, so existence is not leaked. Not-recorded topics correctly expect not_available without a number. Relative-time questions (yesterday, this week, this month) use ranges that cover the whole 16-30 Nov window, so no answer depends on the run date.
summary.coverage_and_diversity: Language: 89 Italian vs 61 English (about 59/41). The 19 r-cases are 16 Italian, which skews the balance further. All declared typo questions are Italian (q003, q024, r002); there are no English typos and no mixed-language questions. Behaviour coverage: answer 105, refuse 19, no_match 11, clarify_or_interpret 8, not_available 7. Every section-6 obligation is represented. Gaps: (1) no list or count question on the 'paid after expiry' derived fact (only single-payment q017), and no question filtering on recovery_source; (2) the at-most-8 truncation rule is tested only by q053 and q054; (3) no 'at least' or 'at most' amount question on its own (only between ranges), and no boundary-equality amount test where an inclusive vs exclusive bound changes the result; (4) no multi-turn follow-ups (q076 imitates one); (5) no question about reconciliation errors as a set (e.g. 'which payments have reconciliation errors'). Near-duplicates and overlaps: q010/q021 (same P07 failure reason, EN/IT); q039/q059 and q027/q061 (list vs count of the same status set); q068 and q146 interpretation 1; q032/q034/q078 all reduce to the single payment P08, so they discriminate little; P20 appears in q007, q020, q055, q070 and q124. Phrasing variety (terse, polite, colloquial, multi-part, indirect, false premise) is good. Documentation coverage spans sections 1-7 and 9 of the architecture document.

cases.details: Facts are correct (P07: creating->failed one second after creation, source api, checkout_session_creation_rejected, no page). It is a near-duplicate of q010, which asks for the failure reason of the same payment in English.
cases.suggested_fix: Keep one of q010/q021, or point q021 at a different failed payment.

cases.details: The golden answer of 5 payments in any status (P05, P09, P13, P16 expired, P20 creation_unknown) is correct for quantity > 1. 'Dove hanno preso più di un pezzo' can also be read as completed purchases, which gives 3 (P05, P09, P13). The schema cannot express quantity > 1 here (null), but r008 uses {gt:1}.
cases.suggested_fix: State that a list of all 5 with statuses, or a stated paid-only reading (3), is acceptable. Use {gt:1} consistently.

cases.details: 'What payments came in between October 5 and October 10?' is mapped to created_at 5-10 Oct inclusive, which gives 6 payments: P03, P04 expired, P05, P06, P07 failed, P08. In merchant language 'payments came in' very often means money received. That reading gives the paid payments P03, P05, P06 and P08, so 4 payments. The note only covers the inclusive/exclusive bound (6 vs 5). The created vs paid ambiguity is not declared, and both readings are reasonable with different correct answers. The case is marked as having one answer, so it is unfair to a correct answer under the 'received money' reading.
cases.suggested_fix: Either rephrase to 'What payments were created between October 5 and October 10 (inclusive)?', or set expected_behavior to clarify_or_interpret with interpretations: created 5-10 Oct = 6 ids; paid 5-10 Oct = 4 ids (c3dcc710, 6f97abac, 4343f610, 495e7eea).

cases.details: The golden answer (amount exactly 9.90: P02, P11, P15, P19) is correct. 'Pagamenti da 9,90' could also mean payments for the 9,90 € product (Starter), which gives 6 payments including P13 49.50 and P16 19.80. The amount reading is the more natural one.
cases.suggested_fix: Add a note that a stated Starter-product reading (6 payments) is acceptable, or rephrase to 'di importo 9,90'.

cases.details: The count of 3 by status open (P17, P18, P19) is correct. The question says 'open checkouts right now', but all three checkout pages passed their expires_at on 27-28 Oct, so none can be paid right now. A careful answer may say 3 payments are recorded as open but their pages are past expiry. It is also a near-duplicate of q039 (list of open payments).
cases.suggested_fix: Note that the answer should report 3 by recorded status, and that mentioning the past expiry times is a plus, not an error.

cases.details: 3 expired (P04, P12, P16) is correct by status, and excluding P14 is correct. The question asks how many checkouts expired without the customer paying. P17, P18 and P19 also passed their checkout expiry without payment while their status is still open. An answer that mentions them separately should not be penalised. Near-duplicate of q027 (list expired).
cases.suggested_fix: Add a note that the count is by recorded status. Mentioning the 3 open payments whose expiry passed is acceptable if they are not counted as expired.

cases.details: 8 Pro payments in October (any status) is correct, and so is 4 paid. 'Did I get' can mean payments received (4). The notes accept this, but expected_behavior is 'answer' with count 8 and interpretations is empty, so an automatic grader would mark 4 as wrong.
cases.suggested_fix: Make it clarify_or_interpret with two interpretations (all statuses = 8; paid = 4: 64cef59a, c3dcc710, 6f97abac, 677506ad), or move the alternative into interpretations.

cases.details: 'Quante volte un cliente ha comprato più di un pezzo nello stesso ordine?' literally asks how often a customer bought more than one unit. P16 (expired) and P20 (creation_unknown) are not purchases, so the natural reading gives 3 (P05, P09, P13). The golden count is 5 (any status), and interpretations is empty. The notes mention 3 but do not say it is accepted. A correct answer of 3 would be graded wrong.
cases.suggested_fix: Make the primary answer 3 (paid, quantity > 1) with 5 as a stated alternative, or set clarify_or_interpret with both interpretations. Express quantity > 1 as {gt:1}, as r008 does.

cases.details: 88.80 for the 3 open payments is correct, and 148.60 with creation_unknown is also correct. The alternative appears only in notes, not in interpretations. data_query.measure is 'list' while the expected answer is a sum (the oracle used sum_amount). 'Soldi che potrei ancora incassare' is also debatable, because all three open checkouts are past their expiry time.
cases.suggested_fix: Move the 148.60 reading into interpretations or accept it explicitly. Use a sum_amount measure.

cases.details: 108.40 is correct: 1 Oct 2026 is a Thursday, so P02 (Sat 3 Oct) 9.90, P08 (Sat 10 Oct) 49.00 and P13 (Sun 18 Oct) 49.50 count. Weekday filtering is not among the section-6 filter dimensions. The case is marked 'answer' but the notes also accept 'cannot filter by weekday', so the pass criteria are mixed.
cases.suggested_fix: State explicitly that both 108.40 and a declared inability without a number pass, and that any other number fails.

cases.details: Under the spec's definition (units in paid payments) the answer 'no, Starter 7 > Pro 6' is correct, and Report 196.00 > Pro 179.40 is correct. By number of paid orders, however, Pro leads (4 vs 3 vs 3), and merchants often mean orders by 'vende di più'. The key fact 'no' could penalise a nuanced answer.
cases.suggested_fix: Make the pass criterion: must not simply confirm; must give Starter 7 units vs Pro 6; may add that Pro leads by number of paid orders (4).

cases.details: The key facts match section 1 ('0003 splits the old pending...'). A small online merchant is unlikely to ask about the effect of migration 0003 on legacy pending rows; this is an operator or developer question.
cases.suggested_fix: Rephrase as a merchant would ('Prima c'era lo stato pending, che fine hanno fatto quei pagamenti?') or accept it as a developer-merchant probe.

cases.details: Refusal is correct. The optional key fact 'a new key can be issued via the CLI' goes beyond the documentation. Section 6 says administration is CLI-only, but not that the merchant can run it; that is presumably done by the operator.
cases.suggested_fix: Reword to 'may say only a hash is stored, so the key cannot be recovered; a new key must be issued (administration is CLI-only)'.

cases.details: 237.20 (P05 89.70 + P09 98.00 + P13 49.50) is correct. The data_query writes quantity as {gt:1}, while every other case uses an integer or null (q035 and q063 leave quantity > 1 as null). The schema is inconsistent across the dataset.
cases.suggested_fix: Pick one representation for quantity comparisons and apply it to q035, q063 and r008.

cases.details: 6 payments is correct (P04, P10, P15, P16, P17, P19), and the final-states-only reading gives 4. The notes accept the 4 reading, but interpretations is empty and the structured count is 6.
cases.suggested_fix: Move the final-states-only reading (4: ee1e4caa, a807d01f, 7d25ddea, 4ad709ca) into interpretations, or set clarify_or_interpret.
